content.text: Confirmatory searches return nothing new: every "access" hit is either Client-side or unrelated to verification. Re-submitting the compliant finding with a sharpened rationale that addresses the false-signal check directly.

input.quote: e. Access. Client will have access to Interface usage statistics and raw log files in real time via the Interface.
input.rationale: No audit, inspection or usage-verification right runs against the Client anywhere in this Agreement, so there is no frequency, notice, cost-allocation or system-access term to cap and no redline is warranted. Confirmed by keyword searches returning no hits for audit, inspect, verify, records, books, monitor, premises, examine and review, and by full reads of the fee provisions (SS 5-6), Client covenants (S 8), the license grant (S 2) and confidentiality (S 10). Every information flow runs in our favour: S 3(e) gives Client real-time access to Interface usage statistics and raw log files, and S 6 entitles Client to documentation supporting charges plus a right to contest them, so TrueLink has no contractual hook for a usage audit. The two Client-side access items are not audit rights: S 8(f) lets TrueLink implement technical anti-spam measures on its own hosted environment, and S 9 requires Client access solely so TrueLink can perform Y2K repairs at TrueLink's sole cost, at Client's request. Neither grants remote or direct access to Customer systems, so the walk-away trigger is not present. The failed deterministic check for an audit-frequency limit is a false signal: the pattern cannot match because there is no audit clause to limit, and silence here is a better outcome for us than the preferred position. Inserting frequency, notice and cost parameters would require first conceding an audit right we do not currently owe, so we take no action and instead flag for negotiation discipline that if TrueLink later proposes a verification right we should hold to once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, TrueLink's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent, and no direct access to Client systems.
